approachQuestion.prompt:
A read-only array of n unsigned 32-bit readings is queried q times. A query gives inclusive indices [l,r]; return the XOR of all readings in that interval. All queries are supplied together and the array never changes.

Constraints: 1 <= n,q <= 200000; 0 <= l <= r < n. Return q words in query order.
Example: readings=[6,3,5,6], queries=[[1,2],[0,3],[2,2]] -> [6,6,5].

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: 32-bit XOR and indexing cost constant time. The returned q-entry result array is output; preprocessing arrays are auxiliary. No hashing or recursive stack is used.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Build P[0]=0 and P[i+1]=P[i] XOR readings[i]. Answer [l,r] with P[r+1] XOR P[l].
options.feedback: The prefix through l-1 occurs twice and cancels, leaving exactly the requested inclusive range.

options.text: For each query, scan from l through r and XOR the values directly.
options.feedback: Every query is answered correctly, but overlapping queries repeat work that a shared prefix array avoids.

options.text: Build XOR prefixes, then return P[r+1] minus P[l] modulo 2^32.
options.feedback: Arithmetic subtraction does not undo XOR. For readings [3,1] and query [1,1], the prefixes are 3 and 2. Subtraction gives 2-3 modulo 2^32 instead of the required 1.

options.text: Build XOR prefixes and return P[r] XOR P[l].
options.feedback: This omits index r. A singleton query [2,2] returns zero instead of readings[2].

feedback.reason: XORing prefixes at r+1 and l cancels every earlier entry twice and leaves the inclusive range once.
details: Build an extra leading-zero XOR prefix array. For each inclusive query, XOR the prefix ending after r with the prefix ending just before l. The shared earlier portion cancels.
XORing prefixes at r+1 and l cancels every earlier entry twice and leaves the inclusive range once. Use the leading zero for l=0. Prefix subtraction would implement sums, not XOR.
“Build P[0]=0 and P[i+1]=P[i] XOR readings[i]. Answer [l,r] with P[r+1] XOR P[l].”: The prefix through l-1 occurs twice and cancels, leaving exactly the requested inclusive range.
“For each query, scan from l through r and XOR the values directly.”: Every query is answered correctly, but overlapping queries repeat work that a shared prefix array avoids.

“Build XOR prefixes, then return P[r+1] minus P[l] modulo 2^32.”: Arithmetic subtraction does not undo XOR. For readings [3,1] and query [1,1], the prefixes are 3 and 2. Subtraction gives 2-3 modulo 2^32 instead of the required 1.
“Build XOR prefixes and return P[r] XOR P[l].”: This omits index r. A singleton query [2,2] returns zero instead of readings[2].

complexityQuestion.prompt: For prefix-xor-boundaries, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of readings and q the number of queries.
constraints: 32-bit XOR and indexing cost constant time. The returned q-entry result array is output; preprocessing arrays are auxiliary. No hashing or recursive stack is used.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Precompute n prefix words and use two reads plus XOR per query.
details: Preprocessing performs n updates and creates n+1 words. Each query needs two lookups and one XOR. The result array is output and there is no additional query copy.
32-bit XOR and indexing cost constant time. The returned q-entry result array is output; preprocessing arrays are auxiliary. No hashing or recursive stack is used.
“O(nq) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes rescanning each query interval.
“O(q) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: It omits the prefix preprocessing work and storage.
“O(n+q) time, O(n+q) auxiliary space”: The result array is explicitly excluded; only n+1 prefix words are auxiliary.
